metadata.description: Comprehensive fix of n5.docx review issues: Bonferroni (Monte Carlo), wider scan, self-contained code, embedded JSON

fano_normalization_note: The v40.36 confirms the Fano profile is correctly normalized: peak is at epsilon=1/q with value=sigma_peak. The n5.docx review claimed the peak was sigma_peak/(1+q^2), but this was an error. Verification: at q=1, max is at eps=1 with value=1 (so peak=sigma_peak); at q=3, max is at eps=0.333 with value=1. The Fano is correct.
v7_explanation: The v=7 magic value is BELOW the dSph Horigome channels (v=10, 15, 20). A 2nd narrow peak (sigma_1_2=0.5-1.0) at v=7 contributes mostly at v=5-9 (for dSph core formation) and almost nothing at v=10+ (preserves Horigome). UV motivation: Tsai 2022 (arXiv:2008.08608) dark-QCD predicts multiple narrow resonances at Y(nS)-like levels with spacing m[Y(nS)]-m[Y((n-1)S)] = C*[1/n + O(1/n^2)]. The v=7 and v=29.4 could be consecutive levels. The exact value depends on the dark quark mass scale.

channel_set_honesty.lower_bound_sources: Kaplinghat+ 2016 PRL 116, 041302 (arXiv:1508.03339) and Rocha+ 2013 MNRAS 430, 81 (arXiv:1208.0025). These give approximate ranges (e.g., sigma/m > 0.3-0.5 at v=10). The exact value 0.3 is a choice within the approximate range.
channel_set_honesty.upper_bound_sources: Horigome+ 2025 (arXiv:2503.13650) for dSph, Andrade+ 2022 MNRAS 510, 54 for cluster, etc. These are 95% CL upper limits with specific methodology.
channel_set_honesty.window_choices: The 20 channels and their windows are a CHOICE, not a unique dataset. Different choices (e.g., Horigome dSph core [0.4, 0.8] instead of [0.3, 1.0]) would give different results. The v19.2-F framework should be re-verified under different channel choices.
channel_set_honesty.sensitivity: A 0.05 shift in any lower bound (e.g., dSph core v=10 from 0.3 to 0.35) could change the basin size by ~50%. The 20/20 finding is real but sensitive to window choices.
